record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: Do isospin-breaking corrections induced by weak magnetism in nuclear beta decays add coherently over all nucleons, and can they become sizeable in final-state correlations when leading-order contributions cancel, such as in neon-19 mirror observables where a_beta_nu and A_beta are close to 4%?

evidence.quote: isospin breaking corrections due to the weak magnetism contribution are expected to contribute to nuclear decays and give non-negligible contributions to final-state correlations (14).

In cases where a large cancellation of the leading order results occurs (such as for 19Ne where both aβν and Aβ are close to 4%), such corrections might be sizeable. It is unclear whether the isospin breaking corrections sum coherently over all nucleons, and needs further research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In allowed nuclear β decay, the hadronic current receives recoil-order corrections, among which the weak-magnetism term plays a prominent role. The Standard Model prediction for the weak-magnetism form factor assumes exact isospin symmetry between the initial and final nuclear states; in reality, isospin symmetry is broken by the proton–neutron mass difference, electromagnetic interactions, and charge-symmetry-breaking components of the strong interaction. For a given nucleus with A nucleons, let δb_i denote the isospin-breaking correction to the weak-magnetism contribution associated with nucleon i, and let δb_total = Σ_i δb_i be the total correction entering the nuclear matrix element governing the β–ν angular correlation coefficient a_{βν} and the β-asymmetry parameter A_β.

(a) Determine whether the individual contributions δb_i add coherently across all A nucleons (so that δb_total scales with the number of nucleons or with a collective nuclear quantity) or whether they add incoherently (so that cancellations or stochastic-like scaling occur).

(b) For the mirror transition of ^{19}Ne, where the leading-order Standard Model predictions for a_{βν} and A_β are both close to 4% in magnitude and large cancellations between Fermi and Gamow–Teller contributions occur, quantify the size of the weak-magnetism isospin-breaking corrections to a_{βν} and A_β and determine whether these corrections are sizeable compared to the leading-order values.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on β-decay correlations and recoil corrections, including studies of mirror transitions and weak-magnetism form factors, acknowledges that recoil and isospin-breaking corrections cannot be neglected at the ~1% precision now reached experimentally, and treats ^{19}Ne as a special case where leading-order suppression enhances the relative importance of such corrections. No source found provides a definitive answer to whether weak-magnetism isospin-breaking corrections add coherently across nucleons, indicating the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: ft values of the mirror transitions and the weak-magnetism-induced current in allowed nuclear decay
status_evidence.snippet: Weak magnetism is an important recoil term in both mirror β decays and β decays in higher isospin multiplets.
status_evidence.claim: Weak magnetism is a relevant recoil correction in mirror β decays such as 19Ne, but the coherence of isospin-breaking corrections is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Isospin Symmetry Breaking in Atomic Nuclei (MDPI)
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order corrections such as recoil-order corrections induced by the strong interaction and radiative corrections cannot necessarily be neglected at the level of precision (~1%).
status_evidence.claim: Isospin-breaking and recoil corrections are non-negligible at current experimental precision.

status_evidence.title: Isospin Breaking in the Nucleon Mass and the Sensitivity of β Decays to New Physics
status_evidence.snippet: Isospin breaking in the nucleon affects β-decay observables.
status_evidence.claim: Single-nucleon isospin-breaking effects are studied but their coherent summation over nucleons in nuclei is not established.
